faqs.question: What does the AFB-Smear Examination by ZN Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates measure?
faqs.answer: This test measures the presence of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) specific to Mycobacterium tuberculosis in pus, abscess, or aspirate specimens with a special dye.

faqs.question: Why is the AFB-Smear Examination by ZN Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose and confirm tuberculosis infection. • To determine the appropriate treatment for tuberculosis. • To monitor the effectiveness of tuberculosis treatment. • To detect drug-resistant strains of tuberculosis.

faqs.question: When is the AFB-Smear Examination by ZN Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test may be recommended if you have • Symptoms suggestive of tuberculosis infection, such as persistent cough, fever, night sweats, and weight loss. • Close contact with someone diagnosed with tuberculosis. • A weakened immune system due to conditions like HIV/AIDS. • A history of tuberculosis exposure or previous treatment.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB-Smear Examination by ZN Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results, i.e., results showing the presence of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) in the specimen indicate a positive result for tuberculosis infection.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB-Smear Examination by ZN Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates?
faqs.answer: A small sample of pus, abscess, or aspirate will be collected in a sterile container. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for processing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB-Smear Examination by ZN Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates?
faqs.answer: • Collect a fresh sample of pus, abscess, or aspirate in a sterile leak-proof container. • Ensure that the specimen type, site, and relevant clinical history are properly mentioned on the test requisition form. • Follow any specific instructions provided by your doctor regarding fasting or medication restrictions. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the AFB-Smear Examination by ZN Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside the AFB-Smear Examination by ZN Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates include: • Mycobacterial culture and sensitivity testing • Molecular tests like GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay for rapid detection of tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance

faqs.question: What is the AFB-Smear Examination by ZN Stain – Pus, Abscess, and Aspirates also known as?
What is tuberculosis?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis is a contagious bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body. Symptoms may include persistent cough, fever, night sweats, and weight loss. Timely diagnosis and treatment are crucial to prevent the spread of tuberculosis.
